Definition: Decision-support software for open, auditable piping mechanics.
Public mechanics implemented by the solver: geometry, stiffness, loads, stress recovery, units, diagnostics, and reports.
Standards-body text, tables, figures, protected examples, copied code formulas, allowables, SIF/flexibility tables, and protected dimensional tables.
Licensed or project-specific values, formulas, allowables, SIFs, flexibility factors, load combinations, owner requirements, and interpretations entered by the user.
A 3D line-element representation of piping centerlines and components for global analysis.
A user-defined expression or comparison applied to solver outputs and user-supplied inputs.
A deterministic, provenance-bearing downstream package or sidecar set with explicit stable ID mapping, loss reporting, privacy metadata, diagnostics, and professional-boundary notices.
A structured finding for missing data, units, provenance, solver state, rule readiness, IP boundary, privacy, report completeness, or unsupported behavior.
Source, license or redistribution status, contributor certification, and review disposition for reliance-affecting data.
External hash-bound review record, if used; it is not emitted by the solver or rule-pack evaluator.
Software computation of displacements, rotations, forces, moments, reactions, stresses, and diagnostics from the recorded model basis.
A competent person reviews the model, inputs, rule basis, diagnostics, reports, assumptions, and limitations before professional reliance.
Numerical mechanics completed for the stated model and evidence set; does not mean a user rule check is complete.
Required physical data for solving is missing.
Mechanics may be solved but a rule pack lacks required user/code data, provenance, or private inputs.
A user-defined rule pack evaluated available results and inputs.
A user-defined rule pack produced at least one failing result.
Professional use still requires competent human review.
Reserved for an external human acceptance record bound to the exact reviewed hashes and scope; not software approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance determination.
Required physical input is missing or invalid.
Mechanics can solve but rule-pack data is missing.
A value has missing or weak source evidence.
A user/model assumption needs review.
Active-state or convergence uncertainty exists.
Protected, proprietary, private, or unclear data may be in a public/report path.
User-owned or invented-example deterministic, sandboxed, unit-aware computation over solver results with explicit required inputs, unit checks, provenance, checksums, and privacy state.
Selects a local SQLite-backed project store/index.
Makes native JSON, CAEPIPE MBF, CAEPIPE run evidence, stress-neutral CSV/JSON, PCF, glTF review geometry, stable ID maps, loss reports, and adapter SDK surfaces explicit.
